newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 18.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Fidel Ramos said all presidential aspirants should take a one-week crash course in national security administration, undergo a hands-on orientation at the palace and attend at least one Cabinet meeting. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- Officials of the Philippine National Police have mobilised its intelligence operatives nationwide on the possiblity that Filipino-American Philip Cunanan, suspect in the murder of world renowned fashion designer Gianni Versace, may have slipped into the country. (BULLETIN)

- Some 29 student mountain climbers have been reported missing since last Sunday when they failed to come down as scheduled from the 4,111 feet high Mt. Natib in Bataan, north of Manila, police said. (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- The promise of computerised elections for the national elections next year will remain a promise as a bill authorising an automated voting and counting system has yet to be enacted. (MANILA TIMES)

- National officials and politicians including a senator attended the groundbreaking rites of a construction materials company in Pampanga, north of Manila, owned by a suspected godfather of local drug lords. (INQUIRER)

- The peso strengthened further against the dollar on Thursday, nearly a week after it was allowed to decline against other currencies and stocks also rebounded after the Central Bank reduced key short-term rates. (INQUIRER/MALAYA/CHRONICLE)
- The Central Bank on Thursday lowered overnight borrowing rate to 25 percent from 28 percent with the recovery of the peso against the dollar in the foreign exchange market. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The Central Bank asked the Bankers Association of the Philippines to reduce further the four percent spread that banks can impose on their buying and selling rate based on the previous day's weighted reference rate.(PHILIPPINE STAR)
- The Philippines will borrow a total of $1.45 billion from the International Monetary Fund and the Japan's Export-Import Bank to boost the country's gross international reserves. (MANILA TIMES)
